person.name: Zach Sykes
person.summary: Product-focused software engineer building workflow-heavy applications with React, TypeScript, Next.js, and .NET. I build and own production applications across frontend architecture, backend APIs, cloud infrastructure, and observability, with a particular focus on making complex workflows intuitive for users.
person.timeZone: Mountain Time (Denver, CO) — flexible across time zones
person.availability: Open to hybrid and remote full-time product engineering roles, including frontend, full-stack, backend-heavy product work, and internal tools
person.lookingFor: A full-time product engineering role where I can own a workflow from the interface through the API, and stay with it after it ships. Frontend and full-stack work is home base. Also interested in backend-heavy product work, internal tools, and teams that treat reliability as part of the feature. I like partnering with product, design, and the people who use the system. Based in Denver, and open to hybrid or remote.

narrative.originStory: I wanted new challenges, and the work-life balance of kitchen work had run its course. I knew I could do something more mentally demanding — and engineering turned out to be the perfect mix of creativity and structure for me.
narrative.bridge: I quit my kitchen job, sold my car to float the income gap, and went full-time through General Assembly's software engineering bootcamp. Outside of class I logged countless hours on YouTube tutorials, documentation, and side experiments — that self-directed time is what actually made the transition stick.
narrative.carryover: Kitchen leadership is constant quick decision-making (shipping fast and efficiently), tightening systems for reliability, coaching the people around you, and forecasting problems before they happen. That's most of what senior engineering work actually is — different artifacts, same instincts.

roles.title: Senior Software Engineer
roles.summary: Senior Software Engineer since September 2026, promoted from Full Stack Software Engineer (June 2023–September 2026). Owns production reliability, incident response, and end-to-end delivery for React, TypeScript, and .NET applications.
achievements: Own production quality and reliability for critical applications, including incident response, root-cause debugging, monitoring, error reduction, and long-term stability improvements across distributed workflows.
Lead end-to-end delivery of React, TypeScript, and .NET applications, owning requirements and architecture through implementation, deployment, and production support.

Build event-driven integrations across business systems, REST APIs, Azure services, messaging infrastructure, and relational data stores, emphasizing traceability and resilient asynchronous processing.

Drove the transition from Blazor frontends to React and TypeScript, establishing reusable component and API integration patterns adopted across multiple teams and improving maintainability and delivery consistency.
Support CI/CD and production observability with GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines, Grafana, and Application Insights to enable rapid releases and effective production troubleshooting.
Independently architected and shipped a real-time Planning Poker platform with WebSocket/SignalR infrastructure and backend services; adopted across software teams as a reusable internal tool.
Mentor junior engineers on architecture, code quality, debugging, and engineering practices; contribute to team-wide technical standards.

projects.name: Budgeting and debt planning
projects.summary: Personal project I am spending my time on. An app that helps people budget and manage debt, in progress. A Next.js app and ASP.NET Core API over PostgreSQL. Clerk sign-in resolves a household on the server. Manual accounts, transactions, and CSV import work without a bank connection. Optional Plaid linking syncs through a separate one-shot worker; access tokens are encrypted before storage. Source is public at https://github.com/Calathea-Z/Cardui.
outcomes: Screens in the product today: home, accounts, transactions, institutions, categories, budgets, income, bills, and debts.
Income includes sources, paycheck schedules, and scenarios. Bills include recurring suggestions.
Debt summary totals recorded balances, this month's interest, minimums, and utilization of known credit limits. A connected card or loan can be compared with the recorded balance.
Next slice: a manual debt can follow a synced card or loan balance instead of being retyped after each payment. That follow mode is designed and not built yet.
Source is public at https://github.com/Calathea-Z/Cardui. Write-up at https://zachsykes.dev/projects/budgeting

projects.name: Planning Poker
projects.summary: Real-time estimation platform built for distributed delivery teams at Forvis Mazars, integrated with Jira for viewing stories and updating estimates. Replaced manual estimation coordination with a single internal workflow that improved session consistency and reduced meeting friction.
outcomes: Shipped from 0 to 1 as reusable internal tooling, including WebSocket infrastructure, Jira integration, and backend services.
Integrated directly with Jira to load stories into sessions and write estimates and updates back after rounds complete.
Adopted by every software team across all verticals for real-time distributed estimation sessions.

projects.name: zach.dev portfolio assistant
projects.summary: Recruiter-friendly portfolio chat over a structured resume: Next.js chat UI, ASP.NET Core streaming backend, Anthropic integration, request validation, and API abuse safeguards. Built to demonstrate building around AI for an actual purpose — not just experimenting with it.
outcomes: Working example of agentic chat over structured data with a real backend, validation, and safeguards.
Source code public for review at github.com/Calathea-Z/portfolio_ai.

projects.name: Portfolio MCP resume server
projects.summary: stdio Model Context Protocol server that registers the same seven structured resume tools as the portfolio chat (get_role, search_resume, list_projects_by_skill, get_metrics, list_recent_shipped, get_narrative, get_faq). Loads the canonical resume.json via --data for Claude Desktop and other MCP clients. JSON input schemas under mcp/schemas are parity-tested in .NET against ResumeToolInputSchemas so Anthropic and MCP surfaces stay aligned.
outcomes: Same tool contracts as the streaming chat API, exposed at the protocol layer instead of a bespoke HTTP integration.
Public write-up and demo video at https://zachsykes.dev/projects/mcp-server; implementation in the portfolio repo under mcp/.

education.note: Full-time immersive program. Career change from operations leadership into software engineering, supplemented by extensive self-directed study via documentation, tutorials, and side projects.

beliefs: Reliability beats novelty in production systems. New tools are welcome, but only when they reduce risk or improve developer throughput measurably.
Clear contracts matter: typed boundaries, explicit API behavior, and predictable ownership between frontend, backend, and data layers.
Observability is part of feature delivery, not a follow-up task.
Mentoring and code-review quality compound over time and are part of senior engineering impact, not side work.

faq.question: Why did you build this chatbot?
faq.answer: To demonstrate I know how to build around and with AI for an actual purpose — not just experiment with it. This site is a working example: agentic chat over structured resume data, with a real ASP.NET Core streaming backend, request validation, and safeguards against abuse. faq.question: What is the MCP server on your portfolio?
faq.answer: A Node.js stdio server using the Model Context Protocol SDK. It exposes the exact same seven resume-backed tools as this chat so Claude Desktop (or any MCP host) can call them against the same resume.json file—no second HTTP API to maintain. Input schemas live in mcp/schemas and are checked in CI against the C# ResumeToolInputSchemas constants so the wire contract cannot drift quietly. Install notes are in the repo mcp/README.md; a short demo and copy live at https://zachsykes.dev/projects/mcp-server.

faq.question: What's your biggest engineering accomplishment so far?
faq.answer: Two things, both at Forvis Mazars. First, shipping Planning Poker from zero to a tool now adopted by every software team across all verticals. Second, helping lead the migration from a Blazor frontend to React/TypeScript — including the architecture work, the rollout, and the teaching that made it stick across teams.

faq.question: How do you approach learning new tech?
faq.answer: I play with it, build small things, watch tutorials, ask questions, and fail at it until I succeed. Docs and reading have a place, but nothing teaches like shipping something half-broken and fixing it.

faq.question: Why did you switch from kitchen leadership to engineering?
faq.answer: I wanted new challenges, and the work-life balance of kitchen work had run its course. I knew I could do something more mentally demanding — engineering turned out to be the perfect mix of creativity and structure. Quit the kitchen job, sold my car to bridge the income gap, did the General Assembly bootcamp full-time, and logged countless self-directed hours alongside it.

faq.answer: Reliability beats novelty in production systems — new tools earn their place by reducing risk or measurably improving developer throughput.
